operations.evidence: Medical incidents totalled 10,602 and represented 4.9% of non-fire incidents.
Medical response arrangements and trial participation affect comparability over time and place.
Fire and rescue services attended 32,713 road traffic collision incidents, representing 15% of non-fire incidents.
Road traffic collision attendance is network-based and cannot be attributed to a parcel without exact geospatial evidence.
There were 17,502 flooding and rescue-or-evacuation-from-water incidents, including 15,920 flooding incidents and 1,582 water rescue or evacuation incidents.
These categories cover broad incident types and do not prove flood exposure for a specific property.
No-action or advice incidents totalled 21,587 in the year ending March 2026.
A no-action outcome can reflect many circumstances and is not evidence of a safe or unsafe location.
Lift release was the largest category in the remaining non-fire group, with 13,760 incidents.
Lift-release volume is service-demand evidence, not a general public-safety score.
There were 184 fire-related fatalities in dwelling fires, 72% of all fire-related fatalities and 14% fewer than the previous year.
National dwelling-fatality figures cannot be assigned to an individual dwelling.
The 239 fires with at least one fatality represented 0.36% of primary fires.
A national ratio is not an actuarial probability for a specific building and is sensitive to small counts.
The average total response time to primary fires was 9 minutes 25 seconds, 19 seconds longer than the previous year.
National average response time hides local station, geography, traffic and incident-type variation.
The average total response time to secondary fires was 9 minutes 58 seconds, 36 seconds longer than the previous year.
Secondary-fire response times may fluctuate with incident volumes and do not predict response to a parcel.
Incident data were collected through the Incident Recording System until November 2025 and through the Fire and Rescue Data Platform from then onward.
A system transition can affect data continuity and requires caution in time-series interpretation.
The published figures use incidents up to the end of March 2026 submitted by 12 May 2026, and later revisions may occur.
The release is a database snapshot and may differ from later local records, especially for small counts.
Suffolk Fire and Rescue Service could not submit all incidents between September 2024 and June 2025, so figures for that period are underestimated.
Affected Suffolk comparisons must be treated as incomplete and cannot support high-confidence local scoring.
The release is identified as accredited official statistics under the Code of Practice for Statistics.
Accreditation supports production quality but does not make national aggregates parcel-level evidence.

Primary fires include incidents in non-derelict buildings, vehicles or outdoor structures, incidents involving a fatality, casualty or rescue, or incidents attended by five or more pumping appliances.
The classification is operational and does not by itself quantify severity or risk for any particular property.
All 30 wave53 source IDs are unique and use a new indexed prefix.
Zero source roles were promoted to exact-address evidence, parcel risk, candidate values or business rows.
30 source rows and 64 operation rows were prepared for line-by-line website visibility.
No second runner, queue replacement, runtime execution, database write or business-data write was performed.
